subject: Post-call: token burn drivers, quick wins & budget runway
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@paypilot.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: token burn drivers, quick wins & budget runway

Thanks again for the time today, Oliver — good conversation. Quick written recap so we have alignment and clear next steps.

Key pain points you reiterated:
- High token spend driven by: long conversational prompts + dense embedding lookups for risk scoring, and a separate reranker call per candidate.
- User-perceived latency spikes when the downstream search tier falls back (duplicates requests).
- Current caching is limited (per-request, no KV cache across sessions) and ops prefer minimal infra changes.

Stated goals:
- Reduce per-endpoint token cost ~50–60% without degrading MRR-facing quality metrics.
- Maintain p95 inference latency under ~200ms for the gateway path.
- Pilot must fit within an initial budget envelope of ~$18k/month for the first 90 days.

Lever candidates we discussed (prioritized):
1) Continuous batching on the embedding / rerank path (low lift on Redwood side, 20–35% token cost improvement expected depending on latency SLOs).
2) Persistent prefix / KV caching for session prompts (helps when users repeat patterns — 15–25% further savings).
3) Model variant strategy (quantized reranker or smaller reranker model for non-critical candidates).
4) Smarter fallbacks: degrade to cached reply + asynchronous enrichment for non-blocking UX.
5) Rate-based routing: stub lower-cost model for heavy tails.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- I attached a first-pass cost workbook (paypilot_cost_model_v1.xlsx) with baseline math and two pilot sizing options. Please review the baseline tokens/req assumptions and update where ours differ.
- If you can send exact average tokens per request (search + rerank) and hourly traffic profile, we’ll run a scenario that shows expected monthly spend and savings bands.
- Ben will map a rough pilot pricing/commit path and provide a ballpark SOW.

Proposed timeline:
- Week 1: validate token assumptions (you) + Redwood to run scenario variants
- Week 2: finalize pilot scope & publish SOW draft
- Week 3: pilot kickoff (2–4 week duration)

If that aligns, please reply with the three datapoints below and I’ll turn around the scenarios by EOD Thu:
- avg tokens/transaction (search + rerank)
- avg daily active users / peak hourly QPS
- confirmation of $18k/month pilot cap (or adjusted number)

Thanks — I’ll hold Wed/Thu afternoons next week for a quick scheduling call.

— Kimberly Park

Kimberly — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few quick points from our side and adding numbers you asked for.

Quick clarifications:
- We don’t currently have a persistent KV cache; our app sends full context (300–700 tokens on average) and then runs a 150–300 token embedding + 600–900 token reranker output depending on the flow.
- Average tokens/request (full flow) today: ~1,050 tokens. Reranker alone is ~550 tokens.
- Peak hourly QPS: 28 during settlement windows; avg hourly ~9.
- We need the pilot to be demonstrably <= $20k/month — finance is strict on runway.

On SOC2/security: finance asked to confirm that Redwood can provide SOC2 Type II snapshot and ingestion controls for piloted logs — happy to receive a pointer.

Confirming we’ll review the attached workbook and get you the raw hourly QPS CSV by EOD tomorrow.

— Oliver Grant

Oliver — appreciate the numbers, that’s helpful. A couple of pragmatic ballots from pricing/ops that we can run in the model:

Ballpark pilot options (rough):
- Low-touch pilot (no infra changes): Redwood-hosted, routing + batching optimizations only. Expected token reduction 20–30%. Pilot price target: $12k–$16k/month for the captured traffic profile.
- Moderate pilot (batching + KV cache + quantized reranker): Expected 40–55% token savings on peak flows. Pilot price target: $16k–$20k/month with a scoped SLA.

For sizing we used your ~1,050 tokens/req and peak 28 QPS but also modeled a burst up to 40 QPS for settlement windows. With the moderate pilot assumptions we hit ~45% median savings on the workbook. Important: savings scale nonlinearly as cache hit-rate climbs; a 30% cache hit lifts savings substantially.

I attached a one-page pilot SOW sketch and a short note on what we need from PayPilot engineering to make the KV caching non-invasive. If you can confirm which pilot option looks realistic ($12–16k vs $16–20k), we’ll convert this into a draft SOW and pricing table.

— Ben Carter
